runtime.interpretation: 正文仅前向计算，不更新参数；canonical 仅部分反向传播。有限检查和演示退出 0 不能证明完整 GPT-2 训练正确。

source_risks.title: Documentary training does not train, canonical training is partial
source_risks.summary: Original documentary train_mini_gpt only runs forward/loss on random windows: no gradients, optimizer or parameter changes. With identical seed, every parameter array is byte-identical before/after three steps. Canonical adds partial backward: updates FFN, second LayerNorm, final LayerNorm and output-side tied token embedding gradient; it omits attention derivatives/updates, first LayerNorm updates, position embeddings and the input-embedding contribution to tied weights. Independent finite snapshots confirm unchanged attention/ln1/position arrays. Neither is full from-scratch GPT-2 training.

source_risks.title: Supplied architecture differs from exact GPT-2
source_risks.summary: It replaces GELU with ReLU, has no attention projection biases or dropout, and defaults to NumPy float64 allocations. Comment calling ReLU a GELU approximation is pedagogical shorthand, not equality. Full GPT-2/GPU-scale equivalence and full gradient coverage are not established by this code.

source_risks.title: Parameter table component sum is inconsistent
source_risks.summary: The listed per-block entries sum to 7,080,960. Summing twelve such blocks, the embedding entries and final LayerNorm yields 124,356,864, not stated 124,438,272. Canonical arithmetic including FFN biases but excluding attention biases gives 124,402,944. No default 124M model was allocated; arithmetic and a tiny-model count were independently checked. All source table numbers remain unchanged.

source_risks.title: KV cache narrative omits the new token K and V
source_risks.summary: At decoding a new token requires its own K and V and appending them, as well as Q. Looking up only previous K/V is insufficient for causal self-attention including self. Source code has no cache; generation re-evaluates the full cropped context. Exercise cache implementation remains learner work.

source_risks.title: Complexity statements need scope and fixed dimensions
source_risks.summary: O(N^2) per uncached generated token and O(N^3) total describe repeatedly computing full dense attention with increasing unbounded N and fixed model dimensions. Projection/FFN dimensions and the fixed maximum context matter; cached attention still scans previous positions. Finite checks do not benchmark GPU speedup or certify general O(1) decoding.

source_risks.title: KV memory arithmetic versus external model configuration
source_risks.summary: GPT-2 arithmetic is 18,432 values/token and 75,497,472 bytes for 1024 tokens in FP32: 75.497472 decimal MB or 72 MiB. Llama paragraph says 128 layers while canonical memory_estimate uses 126; it uses listed head counts without modelling grouped-query KV-head sharing. Actual Llama configuration, sequence lengths and quoted >10GB were not externally verified here. Memory capacity and bandwidth are related but distinct.

source_risks.title: GPU timing and compute versus bandwidth generalizations
source_risks.summary: Single-GPU few hours, A100 20-50ms and decode time independent of FLOPs lack full model/batch/precision/context/kernel scope. Compute-/bandwidth-bound regimes vary; H100 design motivation is not established by this lesson. A GPU/PyTorch is not a logical requirement for every implementation, but source recommendation is retained. No GPU benchmark or real 124M training performed.

source_risks.title: Residual guarantees, specialized heads and GPT-4 rumor
source_risks.summary: Residual paths aid gradients but do not guarantee every deep network avoids vanishing. Head specialization examples are possibilities, not enforced distinct roles. sqrt(d_k) variance rationale assumes suitable activation statistics. GPT-4 120 blocks is explicitly a rumor in both languages, not verified architecture knowledge.

source_risks.title: Historical training defaults and paper claims
source_risks.summary: GPT-2 2000-step warmup/cosine schedule, initialization provenance, every-major-LLM claim, original paper attributions and current framework recommendations were preserved, not independently verified against external sources in this fixed-source translation review. External reference content was not downloaded/read or used to repair source.

source_risks.title: Single-head attention helper fails on four-dimensional arrays
source_risks.summary: The helper K.transpose(0,-1,-2 if Q.ndim==4 else 1) supplies only three axes. For ndim=3 its tested (batch,sequence,dimension) input works; ndim=4 raises ValueError: axes do not match array. The separate MultiHeadAttention implementation uses all four axes and passed tiny causal-isolation/shape fixtures. No code fix made.

source_risks.title: Mask and shape limitations
source_risks.summary: Source prose describes -infinity, but MiniGPT uses a finite -1e9 additive mask. For ordinary tested scales future positions were isolated; extreme scores/nonfinite inputs/all-masked rows need additional handling. Head divisibility is asserted only in canonical, not documentary code. Out-of-range token IDs and overlong contexts error. NumPy negative indices can have unintended semantics.

source_risks.title: LayerNorm and stability claims are qualified
source_risks.summary: LayerNorm variance before affine is var/(var+epsilon), not exactly one; learned gamma/beta further change moments. Constant input remains finite and maps to beta. Subtract-max softmax is stable for ordinary finite rows, not a cure for NaN/Inf/all-masked inputs. These differences were kept in source explanations and protected code.

source_risks.title: Training data selection and limited loss evidence
source_risks.summary: Training takes only the first 2048 UTF-8 bytes, one fixed-size random window at a time, and randint upper bound excludes the final valid window when enough tokens exist. Short/empty text and vocab<256 byte IDs need guards. Reported loss varies with sampled windows; there is no held-out validation, LR schedule, Adam, gradient accumulation or clipping in the supplied loops. Random initialized models are not exactly uniform, and source example th after t is odd. Plateau alone does not prove overfitting or a universal GPT-4 curve.

source_risks.title: Temperature-zero statement conflicts with generation code
source_risks.summary: The code unconditionally divides by temperature. Zero causes divide/invalid warnings and NaN probabilities followed by ValueError, rather than greedy argmax. Positive temperatures .5/1/1.5 changed entropy as described on a finite fixture; negative/nonfinite values and empty prompts are not checked. No top-k or top-p filtering is present in the supplied generator.

source_risks.title: Context cropping and byte decoding scope
source_risks.summary: Cropping old tokens and recomputing resets learned position indices to the cropped window; this is not equivalent to retaining all prior context or merely adding a KV cache. NumPy outputs are byte IDs only for the 256-vocabulary demo; default 50257 IDs cannot all be directly converted with bytes(). UTF-8 decoding with replacement allows malformed generated byte strings. Full runs complete but do not establish coherent language learning.

source_risks.title: Exercises and metadata scope
source_risks.summary: Exercises 500/1000-step experiments, plotting, KV caching and top-k/top-p are not implemented or validated by this review. Source code/main.rs also exists although metadata says only Python (with numpy); Rust was not read or run. The learner exercise change to 24 layers and 16 heads preserves 768 divisibility but is not simply doubling all sizes. No source or quiz correction included.

source_risks.title: Formatting and site acceptance remain separate
source_risks.summary: The intended italic why is preserved. Chinese bold spans ending in parentheses next to Chinese text and two raw multiplication stars in GELU exercise need actual GitHub GFM observation, not speculative repair. Offline parser executes but produces thirteen empty Chinese heading IDs, so site/mobile/interactive acceptance is not passed. Three Mermaid payloads are byte-preserved; their actual browser layout has not been observed by this reviewer.
